title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
1. MOS 5702, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense
Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Chemical, Biological, Radiological, And Nuclear Defense
(CBRND) Officers are technical advisers for operational and tactical
functions associated with CBRN protection, CBRN response, and CBRN support to
countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD). They support an
organization’s planning process by providing CBRN subject matter expertise
for plans, annexes, orders, and standard operating procedures. CBRND
Officers serving in protection billets develop plans to support their
commander’s schemes of maneuver under CBRN conditions. CBRND Officers
serving in response billets plan and lead CBRND support to the MAGTF and
joint forces. CBRND Officers serving in CBRN analysis billets apply subject
matter expertise to information and intelligence to develop a threat picture
to guide the commanders planning and decision-making cycles. CBRND Officers
in senior-level management billets (MEU, MEF, MARFOR) develop plans and
advise commanders and staffs on requirements related to activates and
requirements to support combatant commander’s CWMD lines of effort and
objectives within the supported area of operations. Marines entering this
OccFld will initially receive a basic MOS 5701, Basic Chemical, Biological,
Radiological, and Nuclear Defense Officer. Depending on the level of
command, CBRND Officers will fill billets as CBRND/CWMD Plans Officer, CBRND
Officers, CBRN Protection Officers, or CBRN Response Officers.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42_, warrant officer (WO) and limited duty officer (LDO) accession
programs.

        (2) Applicants considered for selection as a warrant officer in MOS
5702 must be the rank of sergeant or above.

            (3) Security requirement:

            (a) Active secret clearance. This is required prior to
attendance of the CBRN Defense Basic Warrant Officer Course (BWOC), USMC CBRN
Defense School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

            (b) For CWO4/CWO5: must meet sensitive compartmented information
(SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background investigation
(SSBI)/Tier 5 (T5) investigation. This is required in performance of duties
associated with MARFOR to MSC and joint billet(s).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4), The
Basic School, Quantico, VA within 18 months of appointment to WO.

        (2) Complete the CBRN Basic Warrant Officer Course (A16EGI4), at U.S.
Marine Corps CBRN School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO. Officers will normally
complete the CBRN course immediately upon graduation from WOBC to qualify for
and be awarded MOS 5702. Any 5701 officer who has not completed the CBRN

 1132                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



Basic Warrant Officer Course after two years will be considered unqualified
and subject to termination.

        (3) Additional skill progression and skill enhancement courses see
MOS 5702 MOS road map.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to
reference (ap), Chemical, Biological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Training and
Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) Mid-level Management Marines (CWO3 to WO1) holding mid-level
management ranks perform the related duties from the entry level ranks with
the following additional classifications:

            (a) First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Officer and Administrative
Support Workers 43-1011.

                (b) Occupational Health and Safety Specialists 29-9011.

                (c) Emergency Management Specialists 13-1061.

        (2) Senior-Level Management Marines (CWO5 to CWO4) holding senior
level management ranks perform the related duties from the previous
classifications with the following classifications:

                (a) Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

                (b) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

                (c) Management Analyst 13/14-1111.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Advisor, 0570.

            (2) Operational Advisor, 0571.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
